title: Livestock Rearing, Nutrition, and Health Management

lessons.title: Breeding and rearing livestock
lessons.html:
Breeding and rearing livestock

Livestock profitability depends on reproduction, growth and survival. A manager sets breeding goals, chooses suitable breeds and manages each life stage.

Choosing breeds

  • Match breed to environment: indigenous and adapted breeds such as Nguni, Bonsmara and Afrikaner cattle, Dorper sheep and Boer goats are well suited to many South African conditions, including heat, ticks and variable veld.
  • Match breed to market: feedlot-friendly weaners, wool versus meat sheep, dairy breeds for milk.
  • Crossbreeding can add hybrid vigour; plan the system rather than crossing randomly.

Breeding management

  • Use a defined breeding season so calving or lambing happens when feed is best and labour can be planned.
  • Test bulls and rams for breeding soundness before the season.
  • Manage female body condition; thin females conceive poorly.
  • Pregnancy diagnose after the season and cull or re-plan open females.
  • Keep records of parentage and performance to select replacements.

Key reproduction indicators

IndicatorMeaning
Calving or lambing percentageOffspring born per female exposed
Weaning percentageOffspring weaned per female exposed
Inter-calving periodTime between calvings
Weaning weightGrowth and mothering ability

Rearing young stock

  • Ensure newborns get colostrum within the first hours of life.
  • Dip or treat navels where recommended and keep birth areas clean.
  • Identify animals (ear tags, tattoos) and record births. Livestock identification marks are required by law under the Animal Identification Act 6 of 2002.
  • Castrate, dehorn and vaccinate at the ages your vet recommends, using humane methods as required by the Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962.
  • Wean at the planned age and weight, managing stress.

lessons.title: Nutrition and herd health
lessons.html:
Nutrition and herd health

Nutrition on veld and pastures

  • Veld quality changes with season. In summer, green grass usually meets energy and protein needs. In winter, especially in sourveld areas, dry grass is low in protein, so animals lose condition.
  • Winter licks supply protein (often from urea and oilcake) to help rumen microbes digest dry grass. Urea must be mixed and fed exactly as the product label instructs, with free access to water, because excess intake causes urea poisoning.
  • Summer licks supply phosphorus and other minerals; phosphorus deficiency is common in many veld areas.
  • Production feeding: lactating females, growing animals and finishing stock may need concentrates, silage or planted pasture.

Body condition scoring

Score animals regularly on a standard scale. Condition at mating and calving strongly affects conception and calf survival. Adjust feeding or stocking before condition drops too far.

Herd health programme

Develop the programme with your vet. Typical elements:

  • Vaccinations against locally important diseases, for example anthrax, botulism, blackquarter and lumpy skin disease in cattle; pulpy kidney and others in sheep. The vet advises which and when.
  • Controlled diseases such as brucellosis, tuberculosis and foot-and-mouth disease are regulated under the Animal Diseases Act 35 of 1984; testing, vaccination and reporting rules apply.
  • Parasite control: strategic tick and worm control, avoiding resistance.
  • Biosecurity: quarantine new animals, buy from known sources, control visitors and vehicles, keep fences maintained.
  • Records: treatments, products, batch numbers and withdrawal periods.

Welfare

Provide water, feed, shelter, handling facilities and humane handling. Low-stress handling improves productivity and safety.

Key points

  • Choose breeds suited to the environment and market.
  • Use a defined breeding season and track reproduction indicators.
  • Ensure colostrum, identification and humane rearing practices.
  • Supplement veld seasonally with licks; use urea strictly per label.
  • Run a vet-designed herd health programme with records.
